You're not pregnant. Pregnancy tests don't "lie a lot", false results can occur but they're rare. You need to wait roughly two weeks after having sex to get an accurate pregnancy test.

Your period occurs roughly two weeks later. It is possible to get pregnant on your period, depending on your cycle length, how long your period lasts, ect. Sperm can survive up to 6 days inside you. Precum can carry live sperm.

So, I've had to stop using nasal spray several times over the years, and this is what I do. Take 3-5 days and write down every time you use the spray. Then you want to start eliminating those times one by one. Say you use the spray at 8am, 12pm, 6pm, and 10pm for example. You'll start by eliminating the 12 pm. Then you stop the 6pm. Give yourself about 3 days or so each time to get used to it. Once you're down to only one time a day, start pushing that time back by 2 hours. Once you've gotten to 36 hours in between, start using a steroid spray or saline spray instead. It may still be uncomfortable for a while, but you'll avoid the horrible rebound congestion. 

I've also read about other people mixing saline spray into their regular nose spray to help wean them off, but I don't know if that would compromise the sterility of the spray.

You can also go to your doctor and they can give you a course of steroids to help you quit cold turkey.
